target_customer: Early stage fintechs, Web3 companies, banks and crypto exchanges that need crypto custody, trading, card issuing and banking
problem: Building a compliant crypto and banking product requires licences and a compliance program that most startups and mid-size firms cannot afford to build.
business_model: Usage-based API with a single contract covering regulated services

founders.name: Prashanth Balasubramanian
founders.background_notes: Early Bitcoin enthusiast and developer. YC page says the company began after he faced banking access problems as an immigrant in Europe. Company was first called Lastbit, a consumer Bitcoin Lightning neo-bank.

technical_complexity.rationale: Combining custody, trading, IBAN banking and card issuing behind one API meant integrating several regulated providers, plus licensing, with a small team.

defensibility.rationale: The company said it held an Estonian VASP licence (and a later report says it was first licensed under the Estonian framework in 2022), which was a licensing barrier, but the API layer itself was copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: OpenPayd launched a banking and payments API for digital currency businesses in 2020. Striga was ultimately bought by Lightspark in October 2025, which made its Tallinn office its European base.

market_need_then: Crypto businesses in Europe needed banking access and regulatory cover as rules tightened; Striga's own pitch says compliance had become a large barrier compared with a few years earlier. No independent demand data was found.

branding.domain_note: Company's launch post says buying the lastbit .com domain would have cost millions, so products moved under striga.com instead.

identity.logo: Indigo horizontal wordmark; a plain S mark appears on profiles
identity.visual_style: Clean modular site with product and card illustrations
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and developer focused, with some playful copy about not reinventing the wheel and APIs that are not horribly documented.

rebrands.why: Company said it did not want to pay millions for the lastbit .com domain; the legal entity stayed Lastbit while products moved to Striga. Exact date not confirmed.

brand_strength.rationale: Known mainly inside European fintech and crypto circles, with partner coverage such as Bitwala and Nuri; no press about the brand itself.

pivots.to: Striga B2B crypto and banking API
pivots.why: YC page frames Lastbit as the initial consumer product and Striga as the compliant infrastructure; the exact date and stated reason were not found.

outcome_analysis: Striga moved from a consumer Bitcoin neo-bank called Lastbit to a B2B API selling compliant crypto and banking rails, and held an Estonian licence at a time when European rules were tightening. It reached 30 countries and a team of about 14 and was acquired by Lightspark in October 2025 for undisclosed terms, so the outcome is a licence and team driven acquisition.
notes: Funding figures conflict and are unverified: Cypherhunter (aggregator) says 3M seed in March 2021 with Binance X, Fulgur Ventures, SkyDeck and others; CB Insights says 470K over 6 rounds; Signalbase shows 1.2M that may be another company. Fulgur Ventures announced an investment in Lastbit in August 2019 with no amount seen. None recorded as rounds. Competitor search returned only undated vendor pages plus OpenPayd (2020), so the list is left empty. Pivot and rebrand dates are approximate.
